Clara: FYI I ran a cross-benchmark comparison for rk-v4 (fp16) vs rk-v4-ptq-int8 across three holdouts: head_anchor, longtail_synth, and live-sampled. Results are weird: head_anchor NDCG +2.4%, longtail_synth NDCG -1.2%, live-sampled MRR -2.0%. Metrics don't move consistently.
Diego: Interesting. Which exact evaluation harness and seed? And did you keep candidate generation identical?
Clara: Eval command: ```./eval_rerank --model rk-v4-ptq-int8 --anchors head_anchor,longtail_synth,live-sampled --candidates 120 --seed 101 --metrics ndcg,mrr,top1_swap``` Candidate generation used the standard prod sampler binary.
Yara: Two axes to isolate: (A) dataset composition (head vs tail), (B) candidate pool parity (we must ensure prod sampler deterministic flags). Also consider whether the PTQ quant made the scorer less confident on long queries.
Luca: Add (C) prompt/priming differences: head_anchor items are often short, longtail_synth has verbose context with many special tokens. Quant can amplify padding/truncation effects.
Clara: I computed per-length bucket deltas. Short queries (<=8 tokens): NDCG +2.8%. Medium (9-32): NDCG +0.2%. Long (>32): NDCG -3.1% and MRR -3.7%. So length correlates.
Diego: That suggests sequence-length-dependent kernel behavior after quant. Do we have kernel selection logs for ptq runtime so we can see if different int8 kernels were used on long sequences?
Clara: Yes I pulled runtime logs. For long sequences runtime picks kvpack-v2-int8 which uses different sliding-window accumulators. Could be precision loss there.
Yara: Action plan: 1) re-run longtail_synth with fp16 but forcing the int8 kernel to see if kernel or quant is root cause. 2) run int8 but with per-layer higher precision for key layers (hybrid-quant) to see sensitivity.
Luca: Also run an embedding-only probe to see if candidate scoring drift comes from embed compression or final MLP quantization. Quick commands:
```
# kernel-forced run
./eval_rerank --model rk-v4-fp16 --anchors longtail_synth --force-kernel kvpack-v2-int8 --candidates 120 --seed 101
# hybrid run
./eval_rerank --model rk-v4-hybrid --anchors longtail_synth --candidates 120 --seed 101
```
Clara: Running those now as jobs 6481234578 and 6481234589. Also I dumped top1_swap by length bucket and saw swap_rate_long jumped from 0.041 -> 0.126 for int8.
Diego: Swap_rate spike matches MRR drop. If top-1 swaps increase on long queries it's plausible CTR impact too.
Yara: Do we have any qualitative examples? A couple of long queries where winner changes could hint at where model loses nuance.
Clara: Pasting anonymized example: 
"query: "how to reconfigure occlusion settings for multi-page pdf import"
fp16 top: candidate A (contains exact flag sequence)
int8 top: candidate B (more generic guide)
So int8 seems to prefer broader matches, losing precise token-level cues.
Luca: That smells like logits compression collapsing fine-grained differences. For hybrid-quant we can preserve final dense in fp16 which may restore precision. Also consider a post-quant temperature calibration targeted at long queries.
Clara: Quick status: job 6481234578 (fp16 forced with int8 kernel) shows longtail NDCG -2.9% (similar), hybrid job 6481234589 shows longtail NDCG -0.4% and MRR -0.2%. So hybrid substantially recovers.
Diego: Good signal. Suggest adding a bring-up rule: for models with long-sequence usage >10% of traffic, require hybrid or per-layer fp fallback for top scoring layers before canary.
Yara: Also add a CI probe that runs a length-bucketed evaluation comparing kernels and quant modes to catch regressions earlier.
DeployBot: Canary 2026-03-24T09:10:00Z deployed rk-v4-hybrid to canary-4 (5% traffic). Auto-roll policy: rollback if long-query CTR <= -1.5% over 30m.
Clara: I'll write up results and propose two short-term mitigations: (1) enable hybrid quant for models serving >X long queries, (2) add length-aware temperature rescale as a quick patch. Long-term: improve quant calibration for sliding-window kernels.
Luca: I'll open PRs and CI tasks for the probes and add the checklist entry.
Clara: Thanks team. I'll post the final numbers when canary runs for 30m. :white_check_mark:
